messages.subject: Re: multispecies modeling error and observation
messages.body_plain:
Dear Oscar and Dakota,

Thanks for reporting this bug. Wallace v1.9.3-7, the dev version <https://github.com/wallaceEcoMod/wallace/commits/master>, should fix this issue.

Please, let me know if the jackknife partition is working again.

Best,
Gonzalo

On Friday, July 8, 2022 at 1:26:04 PM UTC-5 sald...@gmail.com wrote:
> Thank you both!
>
> I appreciate the tip.
>
> I will continue working on the models with that workaround.
>
> Cheers,
> Oscar
>
> El viernes, 8 de julio de 2022 a las 12:08:22 UTC-5, Wallace Ecological Modeling App escribió:
> > Hi to both-
> > We're working on fixing this issue. We've run into it before when a locality falls on or near the edge of a raster pixel and they aren't removed by Wallace but are getting removed during partitioning. If I remember correctly, it's an issue with the raster package so we are trying to transfer all our functions over to using terra, but I will check with the other developers.
> > In the meantime, the workaround is as Dakota mentioned- using another partitioning method. I'll report back when I hear more from the team on this.
> >
> > -Bethany
> >
> > On Thursday, July 7, 2022 at 10:25:06 PM UTC-4 dro...@asu.edu wrote:
> > > Just writing to tag on that I am running into the same error when I use jackknifing, but have circumvented it by now by using k-fold validation.
> > >
> > > On Tuesday, July 5, 2022 at 4:15:26 PM UTC-7 sald...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > > Hi,
> > > >
> > > > I am trying to use wallace to model multiple species, and I got the following error:
> > > >
> > > > Warning: Error in ENMeval : : ENMevaluate: Removal of cell duplicates caused one or more partition groups to be missing. Please make sure all partition groups are represented by at least one non-duplicate occurrence record.
> > > > 2: shine : : runApp
> > > > 1: run_wallace
> > > >
> > > > I am using jacknife k=n and I have previously thin my occurrences to 5km plus using the 5km cell resolution and wallace said before it had removed duplicate cells.
> > > >
> > > > After doing this, the screen is gray and it does not continue. Any suggestions?
> > > >
> > > > As an observation, when you are using multiplespecies, and you delimit the background points, if you use one amount it will use it for all of the species (if you select batch). Wouldn't it be better to select batch, and you get a message that it tells you how much background points can be generated for all of the species and let you decide if you want that quantity or modify it rather than doing it one by one (making the batch function not useful)?
> > > >
> > > > Cheers,
> > > > Oscar

messages.body_plain:
Hi Dakota,

I hope that everything is going well.

Thanks for reporting this issue also. Knowing that this does not happen in the dev version, which should replace the CRAN version in some months, I am not sure to diagnose it for v1. Dakota, are you planning to use the dev version for your fall course?

Best,
Gonzalo

On Friday, July 8, 2022 at 8:22:49 PM UTC-5 dro...@asu.edu wrote:
> Dear Bethany,
>
> Good to "see" you again, and thanks for the help. My version of knitr and rmarkdown were up to date - I forced an update and still received the error. However, installing Wallace v2 solved the problem. Thank you!
>
> Dakota
>
> On Fri, Jul 8, 2022 at 11:18 AM Wallace Ecological Modeling App <wallac...@googlegroups.com> wrote:
> > Hi Dakota,
> > I followed your workflow and was not able to reproduce the error (I've attached a sample RMD I was able to generate). I will flag Gonzalo to take a look at the error when he is back from vacation.
> > In the meantime try updating the 'knitr' package. Also, if you are interested, you can also try updating to Wallace v2 and see if that version also gives you issues downloading the session code. It's a developmental version, but you should be able to run your workflow without issues. You can find instructions on how to install here <https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://wallaceecomod.github.io/wallace/articles/tutorial-v2.html*setup__;Iw!!IKRxdwAv5BmarQ!aTuWEe2Ckacn1Vnnb-SfKcQK65cQzzCWFvO0VXXEQAOXbPmcSp6vdqxbWJKbcKIJOr5Ig9YnPu7FH2BSK0StNYFsdGE$>. The only difference is you will need to edit the csv of your occurrence data; the column header 'name' will need to be changed to 'scientific_name' to work properly.
> >
> > -Bethany
> > PS: Just to put a face to the Wallace account, we met at the sky island panel discussion at ASM
> >
> > On Thursday, July 7, 2022 at 11:00:01 PM UTC-4 dro...@asu.edu wrote:
> > > Hello!
> > >
> > > First of all, I wanted to say that I'm excited to use this program to help develop lab activities for the course I am teaching this fall. I am working on developing example files and learning how to use the program and am running into an error in downloading the output code from the model.

> > > The error I am getting is
> > > "Warning in options$echo && options$ eval :
> > > 'length(x) = 3 > 1' in coercion to 'logical(1)'
> > > Quitting from lines 399-401 (userReport2.Rmd)
> > >
> > > Warning: Error in if: the condition has length > 1
> > > [No stack trace available]
> > >
> > > I am attaching the following files:
> > > Output from the R Console, including the results from the object "version"
> > > The input .csv file I am using for running wallace
> > > The steps I am taking in the program are as follows:
> > > Step 1: Module User-specified: input - attached .csv
> > > Step 2: Remove occurrences by ID: Remove OccID 489
> > > Step 3: WorldClim BioClims: 30 arcsec
> > > Step 4a: Select Study Region: 0.5 degree bounding box
> > > Step 4b: 10000 samples
> > > Step 5: Non-spatial partitions: 4 k-folds
> > > Step 6: BioClim
> > > Step 7: Map prediction: No threshold (but .Rmd error message is unchanged regardless of which method I choose)
> > > Session Code: Download Session Code (does not matter which output I select).
> > > Thanks for any assistance you can offer. I updated all packages today and still run into the same error message.
> > >
> > > Sincerely,
> > > Dakota
